explanation: 该论文研究利用卫星激光雷达观测（CALIOP）数据结合数值模型，构建东亚地区污染的三维分布图，重点关注气溶胶成分的垂直分布及其对大气加热率的影响。这与大气环境遥感技术密切相关，涉及空气污染监测、卫星观测、大气成分分析和气溶胶反演等领域。
authors: Yueming Cheng;Tie Dai;Daisuke Goto;Keiya Yumimoto;Tomoaki Nishizawa;Rei Kudo;Min Zhao;Akiko Higurashi;Yoshitaka Jin;Atsushi Shimizu;Haoran Peng;Guangyu Shi;Teruyuki Nakajima
title: Constraining the vertical profiles of aerosol component and heating rate over east Asia through  assimilating CALIOP observations
abstract:
To understand how air pollution affects climate, we must know where different particles reside in the sky. We combined satellite lidar measurements of specific particle types with a numerical model to build a three-dimensional map of pollution over East Asia. Our method successfully located hidden layers of heat-absorbing soot high in the atmosphere that previous models missed. This greatly improves our ability to calculate how these particles trap sunlight and alter regional temperatures. 
 The vertical distribution of distinct aerosol components fundamentally governs atmospheric shortwave heating rates and radiative effects. However, traditional data assimilation (DA) methods typically rely on total aerosol optical thickness (AOT) or extinction, which fails to constrain the specific aerosol composition and often leads to the misallocation of aerosol between scattering and absorbing species. To address this limitation, we develop a component-resolved data assimilation system based on the local ensemble transform Kalman filter (LETKF) with spatial and observational constraints within the WRF-Chem model. This novel system assimilates CALIOP-MODIS synergistic retrievals of species-specific extinction profiles (dust, sea salt, black carbon, and water-soluble aerosols) to explicitly optimize the three-dimensional distributions of individual components over East Asia. Results demonstrate that this DA system successfully reconstructs the complex vertical layering of multi-component aerosols. Notably, it effectively corrects severe underestimations of elevated black carbon (BC) plumes, capturing persistent free-tropospheric BC layers over South Asia that traditional models typically miss. Independent validations against ground-based AERONET and AD-Net lidar observations confirm significant improvements not only in total AOT and extinction but also in the single scattering albedo (SSA). By independently adjusting the mass of scattering and absorbing species, the system corrects local biases in aerosol optical properties. Consequently, the optimized component-specific profiles profoundly affect the atmospheric shortwave radiative heating. The elevated BC plumes induce a pronounced mid-tropospheric warming accompanied by a reduction in lower-tropospheric heating due to the attenuation of downward solar radiation. This study highlights the importance of component-specific vertical constraints for accurately assessing aerosol-induced atmospheric heating and its vertical structure.

explanation: 该论文研究了用于快速测量大气中N2O的机载量子级联激光光谱仪（QCL）的性能评估，涉及水汽校正技术以提高测量精度，这直接关联到大气环境遥感技术和空气质量监测。
topic_words: ['N2O', 'airborne in-situ measurements', 'Quantum Cascade Laser (QCL) spectrometer', 'water vapor correction', 'air quality monitoring']
authors: Leon Knez;Maximilian Eckl;Paul Waldmann;Alina Fiehn;Magdalena Pühl;Oleg Aseev;Glenn S. Diskin;Joshua P. DiGangi;Yonghoon Choi;Jason A. Miech;Ryan Bennett;Charles K. Gatebe;Jonathan M. Dean-Day;Rajesh Poudyal;Gangwoong Lee;Jeonghwan Kim;Anke Roiger
title: Airborne performance assessment of the DLR MIRO MGA3 quantum cascade laser spectrometer for fast N2O measurements
abstract:
To mitigate N2O emissions, the processes behind the emissions need to be well understood. Because of this, we developed a new measurement setup for precise and simultaneously fast airborne in-situ N2O measurements. We developed an empirical water vapor correction enabling measurements in regions with high humidity and found no significant influence of different flight parameters on the measurements during two campaigns. This setup can help to measure N2O in humid and undersampled regions. 
 Nitrous oxide (N2O) is the most dominant precursor of ozone-depleting substances and the third  most important anthropogenic greenhouse gas, with agriculture contributing the largest share of emissions (56 %). Over the past two decades, airborne in-situ measurements have become increasingly important for studying emission and transport of N2O in the atmosphere, also driven by the development of more precise and simultaneously faster Quantum Cascade Laser (QCL)-based spectrometers.However, many QCL-based spectrometers exhibit sensitivities to environmental and flight-related parameters that can vary rapidly (≤ 1 s), such as static or cabin pressure and aircraft roll and pitch angles. The impact of changing ambient water vapor is particularly critical due to both dilution and quantum-mechanical effects. Because the variability of N2O in the lower troposphere  is often very small (< 1 ppb) relative to its high background (∼ 338 ppb), even minor variations in these parameters can significantly affect data quality and must be corrected. Although many instruments can resolve such small concentration changes, their typical temporal resolution of 1 Hz may limit the application of advanced measurement techniques such as eddy covariance on fast-moving aircraft.Here, we present and evaluate a new instrument setup for precise (< 0.2 ppb) and high-frequency (10 Hz) airborne in-situ N2O measurements in altitudes up to 4500 m based on a MIRO MGA3 QCL spectrometer (MIRO Analytical AG). The instrument was successfully deployed during two airborne science missions, namely onboard the unpressurized DLR Cessna during the Greenhouse Gas Monitoring (GHGMon) campaign in 2023 in the Netherlands, as well as onboard the NASA DC-8 during the Airborne and Satellite Investigation of Asian Air Quality (ASIA-AQ) campaign in 2024. Specifically, we evaluate and compare different water vapor correction approaches using ASIA-AQ data sampled within the tropical boundary layer over South Korea, the Philippines, Thailand and Taiwan, which partly were characterized by specifically high ambient humidity (up to 30 000 ppm H2O). The water vapor correction methods include an empirical approach that relies on both native and corrected MIRO in-flight water vapor measurements, as well as an approach by an updated version of the MIRO specific fitting software. Comparison with N2O measurements from a well-established instrument onboard the NASA DC-8 shows agreement within combined measurement uncertainties for all tested water vapor correction approaches, albeit special caution is needed for humidities larger than 15 000 ppm. The new water vapor corrected data shows a 42 % better precision than with original default settings of the instrument. We further show that the instrument setup is insensitive to flight parameter changes such as roll and pitch angle of the aircraft, and allows for stable measurements even under challenging conditions such as in the turbulent boundary layer.This instrument setup enables improved characterization of N2O emissions and sources from the agricultural sector, which is particularly relevant for tropical regions with strong agricultural activity and high humidity, where observational data remain scarce.

explanation: 该论文研究的是利用FY-4M卫星的被动微波仪器进行全天空大气温度剖面反演的技术，涉及卫星观测、大气成分分析和温度检索，与大气环境遥感技术密切相关。
topic_words: ['all-sky atmospheric temperature profile retrieval', 'Fengyun-4M satellite', 'passive microwave instrument', 'channel optimization']
authors: Yu Wang;Xinbin Ma;Banghai Wu;Qiang Guo;Jing Xi;Rui Li;Xin Wang;Xiaoqing Li
title: A prototype algorithm for all-sky atmospheric temperature profile retrieval over ocean based on channel optimization for the FY-4M satellite
abstract:
China’s Fengyun-4M, planned for launch in late 2026, will be the first geostationary satellite to carry a passive microwave instrument, opening a new era of weather observation. To better use its more than one hundred channels, we developed a retrieval method and an optimized channel setup for all-sky temperature profile retrieval over ocean. The results indicate that this algorithm shows low errors while reducing computing time, which is a preferred choice for future operational use. 
 As the world's first geostationary satellite equipped with a passive microwave payload, China's FengYun-4M (FY-4M) is planned to be launched at the end of 2026, ushering in a new era of continuous observation of various geophysical parameters associated with weather processes. To better understand the observational characteristics of this satellite's more than a hundred channels, especially the potential application of its unique temperature hyperspectral channels (52.6–57.3 GHz) and several high-frequency channels (380 and 424 GHz) in the high-precision detection of atmospheric temperature profiles over ocean, this paper proposes a complete retrieval algorithm with a channel optimization scheme, based on information entropy theory and the Bayesian technique. Using degrees of freedom as an indicator, the ranking results of information contribution show that when hyperspectral channels are included, water vapor absorption channels and window channels used to obtain auxiliary information such as water vapor and hydrometeors are more important for the quantitative extraction of temperature profile information than traditional oxygen absorption channels at 50 and 118 GHz. Based on this, a corresponding channel configuration was constructed for all-weather temperature profile retrieval. The results of retrieval experiments show that the root mean square error (RMSE) remains below 0.5 K under clear-sky and cloudy conditions, and is within 0.8 K during precipitation. Additionally, the computational time is reduced by 14 % relative to the full-channel configuration. This suggests that the presented algorithm with this channel configuration scheme is able to achieve a favorable balance between retrieval accuracy and computational efficiency, making it a preferred choice for future operational retrieval systems.

explanation: 该研究评估了欧洲闪电探测网络（EUCLID）的位置精度，使用了靠近高建筑的闪电事件作为验证点。这属于大气环境遥感技术范畴，特别是涉及闪电监测和大气现象分析，与空气质量监测、卫星观测、大气成分分析、气溶胶反演等技术相关。
authors: Dieter Roel Poelman;Hannes Kohlmann;Wolfgang Schulz
title: Evaluating EUCLID location accuracy using lightning events near tall structures
abstract:
This study evaluates the location accuracy of a European-wide lightning detection network using lightning events near tall structures across Europe (2012–2025). A clustering approach identifies strikes likely hitting structures, enabling large-scale validation. Results show a median accuracy of ~125 m, consistent with previous studies, and reveal spatial patterns and temporal improvement due to network upgrades. The method provides a scalable proxy for performance assessment. 
 This study evaluates the location accuracy (LA) of the European Cooperation for Lightning Detection (EUCLID) network by analysing lightning events recorded near tall structures located either on flat ground or on elevated terrain, such as mountain ridges, over a 14-year period from 2012 to 2025. Structures selected for this analysis, either exceeding 150 m in height or situated on prominent terrain like mountain tops, serve as proxy reference points for assessing the network's performance. The methodology involves calculating the ratio of lightning strike densities within 500 m of each structure to those within the surrounding ring extending from 500 m to 2 km. Structures with ratios below a defined threshold are excluded from further analysis, as the absence of elevated lightning density near the structure suggests it does not significantly attract or initiate lightning and is therefore unsuitable for our methodology. Subsequently, a density-based clustering algorithm is used to identify the most likely cluster of lightning events associated with the structure. It is then assumed that the lightning events within this cluster have struck the structure and can therefore be used in the analysis of location accuracy. Results indicate a median LA of 124 m and a 95th percentile of 258 m. These values align well with those obtained from past ground-truth campaigns using high-speed video cameras and instrumented towers. Moreover, the spatial distribution of LA derived from this methodology shows a similar pattern to that of the median value of the 50 % error ellipse semi-major axis reported by the network. In addition, a focused analysis of two well-known instrumented towers, i.e. Gaisberg and Säntis, confirms that the results in terms of LA from this methodology correspond well with findings previously reported in the literature. More generally, an overall decreasing trend in median LA over time is observed across all towers, which is consistent with expectations given the continuous evolution and improvement of the detection network. This analysis underscores the importance of consistent sensor upgrades and optimized placements to achieve high detection efficiency and location accuracy.

explanation: 该论文研究的是利用MODIS卫星数据对中国大陆大气温度剖面进行验证，涉及卫星观测数据与地面观测数据的对比分析，这与大气环境遥感技术（如空气质量监测、卫星观测、大气成分分析、气溶胶反演）密切相关，因此是强相关的。
authors: Wenjie Zhang;Mengxi Qu;Ranhao Sun;Jiarui Zhao;Guicai Ning;Aziz Inamov;Zokhid Mamatkulov;Di Zhou;Bakhtiyor Pulatov;Yuanjian Yang
title: Comprehensive validation of MODIS atmospheric temperature profile data across mainland China using sounding observations
abstract:
MOD07_L2 lacks full validation across China. Using 18-year sounding data (74 stations), we evaluated its temperature accuracy, lower tropospheric stability (LTS), and inversion (TIL) detection. Nighttime accuracy exceeds daytime; upper layers outperform lower. Negative biases exist at 850/920 hPa, especially daytime. LTS is better by day (r=0.74) than night (r=0.57). TIL detection is low (6.6% day, 13.1% night). This guides MOD07_L2 use in related fields. 
 The vertical profile of atmospheric temperature is crucial for understanding energy transfer within the climate system. The Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (MODIS) atmospheric profile product (MOD07_L2) provides vertical temperature profiles at 5 km spatial resolution. However, comprehensive validation of its absolute accuracy – particularly for lower tropospheric stability (LTS) and temperature inversion layer (TIL) detection – remains limited. Therefore, this study systematically evaluated sounding observations collected at 74 stations across mainland China from 2003 to 2020, covering both daytime and nighttime periods. Results indicated that MOD07_L2 temperature-profile retrievals were generally more accurate at nighttime than during daytime and performed better in the upper layers (400–620 hPa) than in lower layers (850–1000 hPa). In particular, pronounced negative biases were observed at 850 and 920 hPa, especially during daytime. In contrast, MODIS-derived LTS was more accurate during daytime (r = 0.74, B = −0.33 K, RMSE = 4.52 K) than at nighttime (r = 0.57, B = −3.59 K, RMSE = 6.78 K). For TIL, MOD07_L2 displayed limited detection capability, achieving an overall detection rate of 6.6 % during daytime and 13.1 % at nighttime. This study provides essential data support for atmospheric science, hydrology, and ecology fields that rely on high-resolution vertical temperature profiles.

explanation: 该论文研究的是全球温度驱动的热弹性位移数据集，用于GNSS参考站，这与大气环境遥感技术相关，特别是与大气成分分析和空气质量监测相关，因为温度变化会影响浅层地表材料的物理特性，从而影响GNSS高度时间序列，这与大气环境遥感技术中的监测和分析方法密切相关。
authors: Ran Lu;Zhao Li;Lingfeng Ye;Peng Yuan;Yanming Feng
title: TED: a global temperature-driven thermoelastic displacement dataset for GNSS  reference stations (2000–2023)
abstract:
Temperature variations cause thermoelastic deformation in shallow subsurface materials, producing millimetre-level signals in GNSS height time series. We release a global dataset of vertical thermoelastic displacement (TED) for ~14,000 GNSS stations from 2000 to 2023. The dataset uses hourly ERA5 soil-temperature forcing and depth-dependent subsurface properties from global soil datasets. It provides station-level TED corrections for GNSS height time series and related geophysical applications. 
 Nonlinear variations in GNSS station height time series include contributions from non-tidal mass loading and temperature-driven thermoelastic displacement (TED). However, a globally consistent station-level TED product has not been widely available. Here we present a global dataset of vertical TED for approximately 14 000 GNSS stations over 2000–2023, generated using a full-spectrum layered finite-element model. The model is driven by hourly ERA5 soil-temperature forcing and parameterized with SoilGrids-derived depth-dependent subsurface properties, allowing within-day temperature variability to be incorporated into daily TED time series that retain seasonal and nonseasonal components. For the 2612 stations with documented foundation-depth information, site-information-constrained solutions agree closely with SoilGrids-based solutions, with annual-amplitude differences mostly about 0.01–0.03 mm and annual-phase differences generally within 1–3°. Sensitivity tests using ± 10 % perturbations in the linear thermal expansion coefficient, thermal diffusivity, and Young's modulus indicate that the amplitude and phase of the annual TED component are stable under reasonable parameter uncertainty. Globally, annual TED amplitudes are mostly within about 0.2–1.2 mm and locally exceed 1.5 mm, with larger signals concentrated in arid inland and continental regions. The percentile-based peak-to-peak variability of the full daily TED series commonly reaches 2–4 mm and locally approaches 5–6 mm. When applied alone to GNSS height time series, TED produces positive WRMS reductions at about 79 % of the assessed stations, with most improvements within 3 %–5 % and the largest reductions reaching about 10 %. The dataset is publicly available for direct use in GNSS height time series correction and related geophysical applications: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21069958 (Lu et al., 2026a).

explanation: 该论文主要关注地下水存储异常的高分辨率全球数据集，虽然使用了卫星观测和环境数据，但其核心主题是地下水变化而非大气环境遥感技术，如空气质量监测、卫星观测、大气成分分析或气溶胶检索。
authors: Chen Zhang;Yifei Fan;Wenxia Han;Yingchun Ge;Jiabei Zhu;Tao Che
title: High-resolution global groundwater storage anomalies:  a 1 km downscaled dataset
abstract:
We created a global monthly groundwater dataset at 1 km resolution for 2002–2020 by combining satellite observations, environmental data, and machine learning. The dataset reveals spatial groundwater variations that are difficult to see in coarse satellite observations. Evaluation with monitoring wells and regional studies supports its use for broad groundwater assessment, while local and seasonal interpretation should be checked against additional observations. 
 Groundwater depletion poses a challenge to water security, but the coarse spatial resolution of Gravity Recovery and Climate Experiment (GRACE) observations limits the characterization of groundwater variability at regional and local scales. Here, we present a 1 km monthly global groundwater storage anomaly (GWSA) dataset covering April 2002–December 2020. The dataset was generated using Singular Spectrum Analysis (SSA) for temporal gap filling, 19 high-resolution hydroclimatic and geophysical predictors, and aquifer-stratified machine-learning downscaling. Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) and deep neural networks (DNN) were evaluated as candidate models, and XGBoost was selected for dataset production based on internal, cross-scale, and in-situ evaluations. When aggregated to the original GRACE scale, the 1 km product agreed closely with the original GWSA (R2 = 0.972, RMSE = 2.10 cm). Independent evaluation used a global archive of 152 069 groundwater-monitoring wells and a 1° spatial-block calibration–validation design. Effective specific yield (Syeff) was estimated from calibration blocks and transferred to held-out blocks before comparison at a common 0.25° grid. For XGBoost, the held-out evaluation yielded R2 = 0.538, RMSE = 0.378 cm yr−1, and Bias = 0.106 cm yr−1. The association between modeled and observation-derived trends remained similar under ± 30 % perturbations in Syeff, although amplitude-related metrics were more sensitive to the conversion coefficient. Standardized time-series comparisons and monthly evaluations of representative aquifers showed better agreement for long-term variability than for seasonal variability. Comparisons with published regional estimates showed close agreement in the North China Plain, weaker depletion magnitudes in northwestern India and California, and a trend-sign mismatch in the High Plains Aquifer during 2003–2013. Experiments using CSR, JPL, H08, and WaterGAP also showed that reconstruction performance and predictor importance depend on the target product. The dataset provides kilometre-scale estimates of groundwater-storage variability under the large-scale GRACE constraint. Local interpretation of the reconstructed spatial patterns requires additional groundwater-level, abstraction, and hydrogeological observations. The 1 km monthly global GWSA dataset is openly available from the National Cryosphere Desert Data Center at https://doi.org/10.12072/ncdc.hydrology.db7323.2026 (Fan et al., 2026).

explanation: 该论文与大气环境遥感技术密切相关，因为它使用地面调查数据（LUCAS）来制作草地的管理地图，并提到该数据集可以支持基于卫星的监测和大规模建模，这与大气环境遥感技术中的地面验证和卫星观测应用直接相关。
authors: Julien Morel;Jon Olav Skøien;Momchil Iordanov;Mattia Rossi;Matteo Marcantonio;Xavier Rottlan-Puig;Linda See;Marijn Van der Velde
title: EU-wide maps of grassland management using 2022 LUCAS grassland and extended grassland data
abstract:
Grasslands cover large parts of Europe and provide many services. Using the LUCAS survey, a large field survey covering the whole European Union, we produced the first regional map based on harmonized field data on grassland intensity and use, their forb-to-grass ratio, and age category. Strong differences in grassland management were found across Europe. This dataset can support satellite-based monitoring and large-scale modelling of grasslands. 
 Grassland is a major European ecosystem that provides a variety of services, including food production, greenhouse gas mitigation, biodiversity conservation or cultural services. As such, it occupies a central position in environmental and food production considerations. Grasslands across Europe come with a diversity of management, from extensive semi-natural and species rich pastures to very intensive single species meadows. As management determines the services provided by grasslands, it ultimately influences the resilience of European agricultural systems. Consequently, there is a pressing need for a monitoring system to inform evidence-based decision-making for a sustainable management of grasslands across Europe. The 2022 LUCAS grassland and extended grassland surveys collected over 29 900 samples across the entire EU27, providing harmonized in-situ observations for various grassland-related information, including their use (meadows, pastures, pastures or meadows) and intensity (intensive, moderately intensive or extensive) of management. We present the regionally aggregated (NUTS2 level) outputs from these surveys, delivering the first EU27 level map based on harmonized, in-situ collected data of grasslands intensity and use management, their forb-to-grass ratio and age category (i.e. temporary vs permanent). A strong zonation of intensity and use has been reported, with high intensity grasslands located in central and northern Europe and extensive ones located in southern Europe. Meadows prevail in central and eastern Europe, while pastures are predominant in western Europe. Highest forb ratio are generally observed in central and northern Europe. Furthermore, weak but statistically significant correlations were observed between forb ratio and management intensity. Permanent grasslands represented the dominant age category. This dataset can underpin Earth Observation-based monitoring systems as well as large scale modelling studies, further strengthening the evidence base for decisions on grassland management and use, and the multiple productive and ecological services they provide. Data described in this manuscript can be accessed at the JRC Data Catalogue repository under https://doi.org/10.2905/JRC.CVXWHE8 (Morel et al., 2026).

explanation: 该论文研究的是全球每日自然强迫温度数据集，用于归因研究，即量化人类活动对历史温度记录的影响。虽然不直接涉及空气质量和遥感技术，但与大气环境遥感技术中的气候变化归因研究密切相关，使用了气候模型（如CMIP6）和再分析数据集（如ERA5）进行数据分析和处理，因此属于大气环境遥感技术的研究范畴。
authors: Robert Fofrich Navarro;Kelly E. McCusker;Steven B. Malevich;Robert E. Kopp
title: GDNat: a global, daily, high-resolution, natural-forcing only temperature data set for attribution research
abstract:
We created a global daily temperature dataset showing what temperatures from 1979–2020 might have looked like without human-caused climate change. We combined historical weather records with climate model estimates of human influence while preserving real-world weather patterns. The dataset allows researchers to quantify the influence of human-caused climate change on observed temperatures in the historical record. 
 Attribution studies quantify anthropogenic contributions to meteorological changes and commonly rely on approaches that compare historical observations with global climate model (GCM) simulations that are driven solely by natural forcing (Bindoff et al., 2013). However, GCM simulations have limited spatial resolution and are biased by parameterized climate processes and uninitialized conditions that lead to the lack of representation of historical meteorological events (Cannon et al., 2015; Eyring et al., 2016; Almazroui, 2021; Zhang et al., 2023). In addition, attributing climate extremes to human activity requires assessing these events in an unperturbed climate system. We address these gaps by developing a novel high-resolution dataset that provides daily average global temperatures over the past four decades without the influence of anthropogenic climate forcing. We use quantile delta mapping (QDM), a quantile trend-preserving bias adjustment method, to remove anthropogenic warming from the fifth generation of the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts Reanalysis (ERA5) using historical and natural-forcing-only simulations from the Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 6 (CMIP6). The resulting dataset consists of historical Global Daily Natural temperature (henceforth, GDNat) records at 0.25° x 0.25° spatial resolution from 1979–2020, providing a valuable resource for attributing extremes and their impacts to anthropogenic warming. We demonstrate a regional application of GDNat by assessing changes in the number of days in the year where daily average temperatures reach or exceed 35°C over North Africa, the Middle East, South Asia, and Australia. We find an average of an additional 15–30 days per year attributable to anthropogenic to warming over the 2000 to 2020 period.

explanation: 该论文研究与大气环境遥感技术密切相关，特别是地面微波辐射仪的快速辐射传输建模能力，以及如何处理云层对观测数据的影响。论文介绍了ARMS-gb v2.0模型的开发与验证，该模型能够模拟云和降水粒子对观测的影响，从而提高大气监测和天气预报的可靠性。
authors: Ziyue Huang;Yi-Ning Shi;Fuzhong Weng;Jun Yang
title: Development and validation of ARMS-gb v2.0: extending fast radiative transfer modeling capability to all-sky conditions  for ground-based microwave radiometer retrievals
abstract:
Ground-based microwave instruments can continuously observe the lower atmosphere, but clouds make their measurements harder to use. We improved a computer model so that it represents how cloud and rain particles affect these observations, and tested it with six months of measurements from two sites in China. The updated model performed better under cloudy conditions without rain, supporting more reliable use of these observations in atmospheric monitoring and weather forecasting. 
 Ground-based microwave radiometers provide continuous, all-weather observations of boundary-layer temperature and humidity, closing a critical near-surface observation gap. The Advanced Radiative Transfer Modeling System – ground-based (ARMS-gb) is a fast radiative transfer model specifically designed to simulate the brightness temperatures observed by these instruments. This paper presents ARMS-gb v2.0, which introduces a hydrometeor absorption and scattering module and an accelerated discrete ordinate method (ADOM) solver for multiple scattering. The model now simulates cloud water, rain, ice, snow, and graupel using optical-property look-up tables computed with Mie theory and the discrete dipole approximation (DDA). The existing tangent-linear and adjoint (TL/AD) modules are also extended to include hydrometeor processes, supporting all-sky retrieval and variational data assimilation. Validation against field measurements from 14- and 22-channel ground-based microwave radiometers indicates that ARMS-gb v2.0 effectively simulates brightness temperatures under cloudy non-precipitating conditions, with the mean observed minus simulated brightness temperature generally within 1 K of the corresponding clear-sky baseline. Compared with ARMS-gb v1.0, which neglects cloud effects, the root mean square error (RMSE) under cloudy conditions decreases by 1–2 K in the water-vapor band, most notably at 30 GHz, where the coefficient of determination (R2) increases from 0.55 to 0.77. In the weak oxygen band, where frozen hydrometeors have stronger scattering effects, the observation-minus-background (O–B) decreases by 3–4 K. At 51 GHz, the RMSE decreases from 5.23 to 3.22 K, and R2 increases from 0.52 to 0.81. Moreover, the results indicate that the DDA model slightly outperforms the Mie model in characterizing frozen hydrometeors at these channels. However, large O–B departures remain during precipitation events, with RMSE values in the water-vapor absorption band reaching 30–40 K, reflecting rain-contaminated measurement effects and atmospheric hydrometeor uncertainties that require dedicated quality control and observation-error modeling before assimilation or retrieval applications.

explanation: 该论文主要关注作物在水胁迫条件下的光合产物分配动态模拟，虽然涉及农业生态系统和土壤水分，但与大气环境遥感技术（如空气质量监测、卫星观测、大气成分分析、气溶胶反演）没有直接关联。
authors: Wei Xu;Wen Zhang;Yongqiang Yu;Qing Zhang
title: Improving photosynthate allocation dynamic simulations  of crops under water stress conditions
abstract:
This study improves the Agro-C model to better represent how crops respond to changing soil moisture. The updated model adjusts carbon allocation between roots and leaves according to soil moisture and growth stage, and also accounts for leaf aging under water stress. Tests with field data for maize and wheat showed better predictions of plant growth above and below ground. The results can improve estimates of crop production and soil carbon storage under future drought and climate change. 
 Accurately simulating crop photosynthate allocation under water stress is critical for predicting both food security and ecosystem carbon inputs. Current crop models often rely on static or growth-stage-fixed allocation coefficients, which limits their ability to capture the physiological plasticity of crops responding to fluctuating environmental conditions. This study develops a water-driven, stage-dependent carbon allocation scheme within the Agro-C model to better represent crop responses to soil moisture variability. The scheme dynamically adjusts photosynthate allocation coefficients for roots (PR) and leaves (PL), integrates the yellow-to-green leaf ratio (YGR), and incorporates a water stress-induced leaf senescence module. By coupling carbon allocation to both soil moisture and crop development, the approach improves the representation of physiologically regulated allocation processes and enhances the realism of crop simulations. Model evaluation using extensive observation datasets for maize and wheat demonstrates substantial improvements in simulation accuracy, with R2 values reaching 0.77–0.95 for aboveground biomass (AGB) and 0.62–0.83 for belowground biomass (BGB). These results underscore the importance of dynamically representing carbon allocation under water stress and offer an improved framework for simulating carbon–water interactions in agroecosystems.

title: Declining Surface Solar Radiation Resources in Polar Regions Under Global Warming
abstract: Surface solar radiation is a key component of the polar energy budget and solar energy resource availability, but biases in climate models limit confidence in future projections. We developed a U‐Net deep learning framework to correct surface solar radiation from 12 Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 6 models using the European Centre for Medium‐Range Weather Forecasts Reanalysis v5 as reference. The correction reduced mean biases by up to 91% and markedly reduced inter‐model spread. Corrected projections under four Shared Socioeconomic Pathways show persistent declines in surface solar radiation and surface solar radiation resources across both polar regions throughout the twenty‐first century, with larger decreases under higher emissions. The Arctic exhibits substantially stronger declines than Antarctica, especially over Greenland and Arctic coastal regions. These results suggest that continued warming will reduce polar surface solar radiation resources and that the Arctic radiation environment is particularly sensitive to greenhouse‐gas forcing.

title: Probing Atmospheric Gravity‐Wave‐Relevant Representations in a Weather Foundation Model via Multi‐Method Fine‐Tuning
abstract: Weather foundation models pretrained on reanalysis data may encode subgrid‐scale physics beyond their forecasting objectives. Using Aurora, we probe this with a multi‐method fine‐tuning framework: agreement across structurally different adaptation strategies signals shared backbone information, while a matched randomly initialized control isolates pretraining's contribution. We evaluate six methods (0.5%–100% of trainable parameters) for predicting ERA5‐resolved, T21‐filtered gravity‐wave momentum fluxes (313–1,820 km). Evidence for a pretraining benefit is strongest for the zonal flux u′w′ ${u}^{\prime }{w}^{\prime }$: several parameter‐efficient methods outperform random initialization, most clearly FISH + TADP (38.9% vs. 41.6% normalized error, p $p$ = 0.007). The meridional flux v′w′ ${v}^{\prime }{w}^{\prime }$ remains hard for all methods (NRMSE 60%–80%). The benefit is level‐dependent: 11–14 percentage points at 200–300 hPa but only 0.2 at 50 hPa. Approximately 1% of parameters recover part of full‐fine‐tuning skill (38.9% vs. 31.8%), indicating regularization by the frozen backbone.

title: Cloud Controlling Factor Analysis Reveals E3SMv3 Structural Bias and Mean State Controls on Stratocumulus Radiative Sensitivity
abstract: We investigate marine stratocumulus cloud radiative sensitivity to meteorological and aerosol controlling factors in a perturbed parameter ensemble of the Energy Exascale Earth System Model version 3 (E3SMv3). The ensemble perturbs 25 cloud, convection, and aerosol parameters, spanning diverse cloud behavior. The default simulation and many ensemble members capture observed responses to most controlling factors, but not to surface temperature advection, revealing a structural deficiency in processes linking stratocumulus to advection. Many members also overestimate cloud fraction and radiative responses to inversion strength, free‐tropospheric humidity, and sulfate aerosol optical depth. Differences in mean cloud optical depth substantially modify the radiative impact of similar cloud fraction changes, showing that the mean cloud state strongly regulates stratocumulus radiative sensitivity. Across the ensemble, conversion of cloud water to rain controls mean optical depth, identifying autoconversion as a key microphysical control on stratocumulus radiative sensitivity.

title: Classification of Summer Extratropical Cyclones Over Northeast China and Their Impacts on Regional Precipitation
abstract: Based on the ERA5 six‐hourly reanalysis data set and objective identification and tracking methods for extratropical cyclones (ECs), this study identified 423 summer ECs that passed through Northeast China (NEC) during 1979–2023. These ECs were categorized into three distinct types using K‐means clustering based on their genesis locations. We further examined the associated atmospheric circulation patterns and the resulting climatic impacts of each EC type on summer precipitation over NEC. The results indicate that: Type 1 (47.04%) originates from NEC and eastern Mongolia, driven by the southward development of an upper‐level trough over the west of Lake Baikal, accompanied by pronounced westerly anomalies. Type 2 (27.66%) originates from western and central Mongolia. Its formation involves an upper‐level trough extending from western Mongolia to the region west of Lake Baikal, accompanied by significant westerly anomalies over central‐western Mongolia and NEC. Both Type 1 and Type 2 primarily track eastward, inducing moisture transport anomalies from the western boundary into NEC, producing precipitation over the northern and central parts. In contrast, Type 3 (25.30%) originates from the eastern coastal regions of China. Driven by a deepening upper‐level trough from North China to NEC and enhanced westerlies toward the Sea of Japan, these ECs move northeastward, steering significant moisture flux anomalies from the southern boundary into the region, producing precipitation over the southern and central parts. This study provides a new perspective on the mechanisms of regional precipitation over NEC.

authors: Basudev Swain;Rui Song;Roy G. Grainger;Marco Vountas
title: Threefold Land‐Use Forcing Intensifies Twofold Warming of Urban Europe
abstract: Europe is warming much faster than the global average, yet the relative contributions of individual anthropogenic drivers to its urban warming remain uncertain. Using CMIP5 single‐forcing simulations and observations from HadCRUT5 data set, we determine the influence of greenhouse gases (GHGs), aerosols from anthropogenic sources (Aaer), together with change in land‐use (LU) forcing on urban Europe's rising surface air temperature (SAT) since 1850. The local Europe Amplification Factor (EAF), the ratio of regional to global SAT trends, reveals that LU forcing has intensified nearly threefold relative to the global mean since the industrial era, driving urban European warming almost twice the global rate. LU forcing exhibits the strongest amplification (EAF≈3.0) $(\mathrm{E}\mathrm{A}\mathrm{F}\!\approx \!3.0)$ compared with GHG forcing (EAF≈2.0) $(\mathrm{E}\mathrm{A}\mathrm{F}\!\approx \!2.0)$, highlighting the critical role of surface modifications in accelerating regional urban warming. Future projections under RCP6.0 and RCP8.5 indicate persistent EAF values exceeding 2.0 over densely populated regions, underscoring the need for integrated emission‐ and land‐management strategies to mitigate urban Europe's amplified warming.

explanation: 这篇论文研究的是马登-朱利安振荡（MJO）如何通过低频海气耦合系统中的风应力异常来激发厄尔尼诺事件。虽然主题是气候动力学和海气相互作用，但它涉及了对大气环境（特别是风应力、海表温度异常等）的分析，与大气环境遥感技术中的大气成分分析和空气质量监测有间接关系，因为这些都是通过观测大气参数来研究气候变化和环境现象。
authors: Jinyu Wang;Mu Mu;Xianghui Fang;Nan Chen;Bo Qin;Chaopeng Ji
title: Optimal Spatiotemporal Perturbation for MJO in Triggering El Niño Events: An Intermediate Coupled Model Study
abstract: The Madden‐Julian Oscillation (MJO) can potentially excite El Niño events by perturbing the low‐frequency air‐sea coupled system through its intraseasonal wind stress anomalies. To fully exploit this dynamic triggering effect, a temporally extended conditional nonlinear optimal perturbation (CNOP) method is implemented within a recently developed, statistically accurate intermediate coupled model that uniquely captures the diverse spatiotemporal features of El Niño. By optimizing additive MJO wind stress anomalies over the constrained space spanned by historical MJO forcings and across twelve neutral reference states from the model’s free integration, the most effective spatiotemporal structures of MJO forcings for triggering El Niño events are identified. When the MJO wind stress forcing is organized with the optimal perturbation represented by the specific spatiotemporal structure of CNOP, it can induce the maximum persistent warming of sea surface temperature anomalies (SSTAs), thereby successfully triggering El Niño events under the operational criterion. Across all optimal spatiotemporal perturbations, strong wind stress anomalies are consistently concentrated in the early stage (January‐March) of the calendar year, even though the optimization target is to achieve the long‐standing SSTA warming in the latter months. Such an early‐year segment of wind forcings in the CNOP is a crucial structure for subsequent SSTA development, as it accounts for the majority of the perturbation’s warming effect. The analysis of optimal spatiotemporal perturbations indicates that the MJO wind stress plays a limited yet non‐negligible role in triggering El Niño events from neutral states, with its effectiveness constrained by the oscillating nature of MJO.

explanation: 该论文研究快速正极性放电（FPB）过程，这是一种云内放电现象，与大气电学和环境放电过程密切相关。虽然FPB本身不是直接的大气环境遥感技术，但其涉及的大气放电物理过程和电场模拟对于理解大气电学现象及其对环境的影响（如雷电活动、大气化学过程）具有重要意义，这些都与大气环境遥感技术有间接关联。

authors: Yuhui Jiang;Mingli Chen;Shaoyang Wang
title: Understanding Fast Positive Breakdown Processes Based on a Macro‐Physical Model
abstract: Fast positive breakdown (FPB) process is a recently identified in‐cloud discharge that produces most narrow bipolar events (NBEs). Existing models cannot fully explain observations of FPBs due to their unresolved discharge physics. Here we develop a macro‐physical NBE model and apply it to investigate FPB processes. The NBE is assumed as a transient streamer‐to‐arc discharge initiated by a weak corona discharge under a locally enhanced electric field. Based on a time domain electric field integral equation, the model self‐consistently simulates NBE electrodynamics such as charge transfer, nonlinear conductance variation, and current evolution. Simulations reveal that the initial ambient electric field is the key parameter governing the discharge. Under specific fields, the model reproduces observational characteristics of FPB, including ground‐based electric field responses, spatial development, and propagation speeds. Results show that FPBs can occur without extremely intense electric fields, requiring average strengths of ∼300 kV/m and local peaks reaching ∼900 kV/m. Such a field profile can arise from a configuration where a compact, high‐density spherical positive charge region above a larger, lower‐density spherical negative charge region. The model also supports that the FPB propagates bidirectionally from the initiation point. The upward negative breakdown is difficult to detect due to rapid decay, while a downward positive breakdown persists longer and dominates the radiation.

authors: Jian Wei;Ping Yang;Ping Chang
title: Tropical Ocean Evaporation‐Temperature Sensitivity to Surface Radiative Property Perturbations in Fully Coupled CESM2
abstract: Tropical ocean evaporation is the dominant source of moisture for global precipitation. However, the dependence of evaporation‐temperature sensitivity on ocean surface radiative properties has not been quantified in the fully coupled modeling framework. This study developed physically based ocean surface albedo (OSA) parameterizations that incorporate multiple governing processes, along with a spectrally resolved graybody effective ocean surface emissivity (OSE). These formulations were implemented as perturbation experiments within the fully coupled Community Earth System Model version 2 (CESM2), and the resulting fractional changes in evaporation‐temperature sensitivity were decomposed into individual contributions via the ocean surface energy budget framework. OSA perturbations drive the large increase in fractional evaporation–temperature sensitivity. The resulting surface warming and atmospheric moistening elevate downward longwave radiation, with enhanced low‐cloud coverage further amplifying this effect. These positive contributions are partially offset by stronger surface thermal‐emission damping and reduced incident solar flux associated with increased cloudiness. OSE modification alone produces negligible changes in sensitivity, as reduced emissivity largely compensates for the weakened thermal damping within the longwave budget. The contrasting responses reveal that OSA adjustments exert substantially greater influence on evaporation‐temperature sensitivity than OSE modifications, operating through both direct shortwave absorption and indirect atmospheric radiative feedbacks. These findings carry practical implications for future Earth system model development. Refined OSA treatments and the associated shortwave radiative budget will likely demand more extensive model retuning, whereas OSE improvements can be incorporated with comparatively less effort.

authors: McKenzie L. Woodman;Edith A. Widder;Warren H. Falls;Joseph D. Ortiz
title: Improving Micro– and Macro–Algae Speciation Mapping for Management: A Field‐Validated Sentinel‐2 and Sentinel‐3 Intercomparison in the Indian River Lagoon
abstract: In recent years, the health of the Indian River Lagoon (IRL) on Florida's east coast has fluctuated due to recurring harmful algal blooms (HABs). These events typically involve cyanobacteria, dinoflagellates, or A. lagunensis (brown tide) causing water‐quality degradation and seagrass decline. The IRL is prone to HAB formation, and they have been observed more commonly in recent years. Although HABs can be non‐toxic, they can threaten critical primary producers like seagrass and destabilize sediments. Due to their impact, it is critical to improve methods of water quality and algal bloom monitoring. To do this, we apply a multi‐image varimax‐rotated principal component analysis (VPCA) to images from a harmonized Sentinel‐2 A/B multispectral imager (MSI) data set spanning three years (2020–2022). Field collected hyperspectral data and a coincident Sentinel‐3 A/B OLCI image is used to further validate the multi‐image VPCA. The VPCA method employs visible derivative water surface reflectance and unmixes the spectral signal to identify orthogonal components related to divisions of algae, suspended sediments, and seagrass. This advances water quality monitoring by improving unmixing and identification of optical components over time. This identification is supported by high correlation to a spectral library, field observation, published observations, and validation across sensors of varying resolutions. Through this research we find confident identification and mapping of in‐water components related to cyanobacterial (component 1 r2 = 0.865) and dinoflagellate blooms (component 4 and 5 r2 = 0.986 and r2 = 0.978), and seagrass beds (component 3 r2 = 0.916) with 10 m spatial resolution through time improving water quality monitoring and root cause identification.

title: Decolonize soil erosion modelling
abstract:
Uncritical extrapolation of soil erosion models developed in the Global North to Global South settings for which they were not designed reflects and perpetuates neocolonial biases in geoscience. To build a more accurate and equitable understanding of land degradation, we must rethink erosion research.

title: Trade-offs between soil inorganic and organic carbon driven by multiple global environmental changes
abstract:
Global environmental changes can induce contrasting responses of soil organic and inorganic carbon, according to an 8-year field experiment in a semi-arid grassland and a meta-analysis. 
 Dryland ecosystems store large amounts of both soil organic and inorganic carbon, yet the responses of soil inorganic carbon to global environmental change remain largely overlooked despite the potential vulnerability of this carbon pool. Here we aim to determine how soil inorganic and organic carbon respond to multiple global change drivers (warming, reactive nitrogen input and altered precipitation) using an 8-year field manipulation experiment in a semi-arid grassland and a meta-analysis based on 44 observations. We found that altered precipitation has no effect on soil inorganic carbon, but warming and nitrogen input interactively affect it. Specifically, nitrogen input alone does not affect soil inorganic carbon, but it increases soil inorganic carbon loss (~9.1%) when combined with climate warming. This inorganic carbon loss co-occurs with enhanced microbial nitrogen mineralization and nitrification, suggesting that enhancement of proton production due to nitrification controls soil inorganic carbon dissolution and persistence. Furthermore, both the field study and meta-analysis show that nitrogen input and/or warming induce contrasting changes in soil inorganic and organic carbon, suggesting a trade-off between soil inorganic and organic carbon under these two major global change drivers. These results highlight the need to account for the vulnerability of soil inorganic carbon when predicting dryland carbon dynamics under future climate change scenarios. title: Direct observation of the Lindhard continuum using resonant inelastic X-ray scattering
abstract:
In metals, the continuum of electron-hole excitations is described by the Lindhard function. Here, the authors directly observe the corresponding Lindhard continuum in the weakly correlated metal MgB2 using ultra-soft resonant inelastic X-ray scattering. 
 Understanding the excitations of quantum materials is essential for unraveling how their microscopic constituents interact. Among these, particle-hole excitations form a particularly important class, as they govern fundamental processes such as screening, dissipation, and transport. In metals, the continuum of electron-hole excitations is described by the Lindhard function. Although central to the theory of Fermi liquids, the corresponding Lindhard continuum has remained experimentally elusive. Here we report its direct observation in the weakly correlated metal MgB2 using ultra-soft resonant inelastic X-ray scattering. We resolve a linearly dispersing excitation with velocity comparable to the Fermi velocity and find quantitative agreement with simulations of the non-interacting charge susceptibility. A detailed analysis and decomposition of the simulations reveal the intra-band origin of this low-energy excitation, confirming it as the Lindhard continuum. Our results establish ultra-soft resonant inelastic X-ray scattering as a momentum-resolved probe of the fermiology in metals. In metals, the continuum of electron-hole excitations is described by the Lindhard function. Here, the authors directly observe the corresponding Lindhard continuum in the weakly correlated metal MgB2 using ultra-soft resonant inelastic X-ray scattering.

title: Three-photon population imaging of subcortical brain regions
abstract:
Imaging large cell populations below the cortex in the intact brain is key for understanding brain function. LIFT, a multiscale three-photon microscope, tracks activity in over 1,500 cells across the hippocampus and adjacent regions in behaving mice. 
 Monitoring large-scale neuronal activity in deep brain circuits is crucial for understanding the principles of brain function. However, existing large-scale cellular-resolution imaging techniques are limited in imaging depth and cannot monitor activity in areas deeper than the cortex in the intact brain. To address this challenge, we developed a Large Imaging Field of view Three-photon (LIFT) microscope with a FOV of  > 3 mm2. LIFT combines high-numerical-aperture optimized sampling, using a custom scanning module, with deep learning-based denoising, to enable population imaging in subcortical brain regions of mice and deep cortical regions of rats. We demonstrate calcium imaging in the intact mouse brain from more than 1500 cells across CA1, the surrounding white matter, and adjacent deep layers of the cortex, and show population imaging with high SNR at a depth of 1.2 mm in the rat cortex. The LIFT microscope offers versatility in imaging scale and rate and was built entirely from off-the-shelf components. Imaging large cell populations below the cortex in the intact brain is key for understanding brain function. LIFT, a multiscale three-photon microscope, tracks activity in over 1,500 cells across the hippocampus and adjacent regions in behaving mice.

title: Passive abortive infection mechanisms targeting phage long tail fiber proteins
abstract:
Cheng et al. characterize two bacterial anti-phage systems that act via either protease-mediated cleavage or kinase-dependent phosphorylation to target phage tail-fiber proteins, establishing the concept passive abortive infection. 
 Bacteria employ diverse defense strategies against phage infection, yet mechanisms directly targeting viral proteins remain scarcely documented. In this study, we characterize two bacterial defense systems: TFAD1 featuring a serine protease and TFAD2 featuring a Ser/Thr kinase. We show that TFAD1 and TFAD2 act on phage long tail fiber proteins via protein degradation and phosphorylation, respectively. Intriguingly, both systems allow complete phage replication cycles but generate non-infective progeny—a mechanism distinct from classical abortive infection (Abi), which we term “passive Abi”. Our findings expand the paradigm of bacterial immunity by unveiling protease- and kinase-mediated incapacitation of phage structural proteins, offering insights into the molecular arms race between bacteria and phages. Cheng et al. characterize two bacterial anti-phage systems that act via either protease-mediated cleavage or kinase-dependent phosphorylation to target phage tail-fiber proteins, establishing the concept passive abortive infection.

abstract:
Coordinating train operations can transform electrified railways into mechanical energy storage for electricity system decarbonization, reducing the need for newly built storage while lowering system costs and carbon emissions. 
 Decarbonizing electricity requires vast energy storage capacity worldwide, but constructing dedicated storage assets creates substantial capital, material and embodied carbon burdens. Electrified railways already exchange energy with electricity systems through traction and regenerative braking, but their inherent potential as mechanical energy storage remains unexploited. Here we show that modulation of train operations can transform electrified railways into Electrified Rail-Based Energy Storage. By analyzing 326,034 inter-stop train operations, we estimate its global potential at 190 gigawatts in 2025 and 315–579 gigawatts by 2050. Capacity expansion models for China, Europe and India indicate that it can reduce investment in conventional storage by 11.9–20.0%, corresponding to an extrapolated global value of US$14.9–35.1 billion annually. Without increasing total system cost, electricity systems with this flexible resource could further reduce operational CO2 emissions by 94.3–258.9 million tonnes per year. Electrified railways can therefore complement conventional storage technologies for electricity system decarbonization. Coordinating train operations can transform electrified railways into mechanical energy storage for electricity system decarbonization, reducing the need for newly built storage while lowering system costs and carbon emissions.
